note: It ends in -a but is masculine: el clima. In Mexico people usually say “el clima” for the weather.
Hace calor = it's hot (the weather); tengo calor = I'm hot.
Hace frío = it's cold; tengo frío = I'm cold.

examples: I like the sound of the rain.
In summer it rains a lot in the afternoon.
note: Infinitive: llover. Está lloviendo = it is raining right now.

examples: There are a lot of clouds.
There is snow in the mountains.
In summer we go to the beach.
In winter it isn't very cold in Cancún.
Spring is very hot in Mexico.
note: In Mexico the hottest time of the year is often spring (April, May).
caliente = hot (food, water); for the weather say “hace calor”.

examples: In Veracruz the climate is very humid.
A hurricane is coming to the coast.
The forecast says it's going to rain.
I saw a huge flash of lightning.
There is a heat wave all over the north.
The rains caused floods in the city.
There was a lot of fog on the highway in the morning.
